scope: Proposition 8.3 of the manuscript “Compatibility entropy and the spectrum of a Thorp sweep” (preprints/Compatibility-entropy-and-the-spectrum-of-a-Thorp-sweep-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dae8f5ca5b99fbec), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n = 2d with d ≥ 1, let Tn be one coordinate sweep, and put Qn = T∗ nTn. Take 1 ≤ k ≤ n/(2d) and consider the representation on functions on ordered injective k-tuples of positions, with g ∈ Sn acting by (πk(g)F)(v) = F(g−1 v) where the notation on v acts on all its positions. Write πk also for the corresponding action of group algebra elements. Call a function harmonic here if the sum in any one coordinate with the others fixed is 0 (taking the sum over the remaining available positions for that coordinate). The space of these functions is invariant under the permutation actions. We claim an infinity norm bound on this space: ∥πk(Qn)F∥∞ ≤  C∗dk n k/2 ∥F∥∞ (F harmonic) (72) with C∗ = 2(4e)2.
